correctness.rationale: For every integer a,b≥1 and arbitrary k≥2, the two payoff inequalities are algebraically equivalent to d_i>b and d_j<−a. Every legal swap shifts exactly two imbalances by ±(a+b), without sign reversal across opposite thresholds; both integer ceiling-ticket totals therefore decrease exactly one. A legal swap exists exactly when both totals are positive. Hence all maximal paths have the exact initial minimum length, and the linear bound follows from type occupancy. Integer verifier reproduced 191080 explicit comparisons and 310832 profile moves; these are checks, not a universal proof.

value.rationale: Exact schedule-independent termination time is a structurally stronger convergence invariant than FIP or a worst-case estimate, with a linear upper bound for arbitrary degree imbalance, a precise equilibrium criterion and a family realizing linear trajectories. A strict improving K_{2,7} swap decreases the standard monochromatic-edge potential; this shows why the problem calls for a new argument, not a routine application of regular-graph theorems.
